findings.text:
SKIP-1: 1 part to fix
SKIP-1[done]: On resume, the dispatch loop skips (via continue) a complete stage whose primary artifact is present after rehydration covers: RESU-3 RESU-4 evidence: core/pipeline/runner.sh:"When resuming, skip stages already marked complete unless --from-stage overrides"
  Given: A run is being resumed; a stage is marked complete and its primary artifact is present in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after rehydration
  When: The dispatch loop reaches that stage
  Then: The loop issues a continue, skipping dispatch of that stage [FIX IN DESIGN: "issues a continue" names a Bash control-flow mechanism, not an observable output; the observable consequence is already captured by the And ("No stage.start event is emitted for it") — say what someone could see happen, not how it is built]
  And: No stage.start event is emitted for it

FRSH-2: 1 part to fix
FRSH-2[done]: A new run of the same issue never skips a stage due to prior run output because the skip guard is conditional on resume_mode covers: GUAR-2 evidence: core/pipeline/runner.sh:"When resuming, skip stages already marked complete unless --from-stage overrides"
  Given: An issue has prior completed runs; a new run is started with no --resume flag and no status=interrupted state file
  When: The dispatch loop runs
  Then: Every stage emits a stage.start event and no stage.skip event is emitted for any stage
  And: Every stage is dispatched from stage 1 without consulting prior run state [FIX IN DESIGN: "without consulting prior run state" describes the internal implementation mechanism (the resume_mode guard is never entered), not anything a test can observe after the When; the observable outcome is already expressed by the Then ("Every stage emits a stage.start event and no stage.skip event is emitted for any stage") — say what someone could see happen, not how it is built]
